title: The Afternoon Brief: Markets in deep retreat; fear index hits extremes
dek: Crypto markets entered a sharp drawdown Tuesday, with Bitcoin down 5.27% on the day and major assets showing extreme oversold conditions. The desk's boards show persistent selling pressure from institutional players despite some signs of bottom-formation dynamics.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: Bitcoin fell below $61,000 as fear gripped markets, but the desk's technical boards show golden crosses and elevated long-to-short ratios across major assets, suggesting possible accumulation building beneath the surface.
bottom_line: Crypto entered extreme fear on Tuesday, with Bitcoin down 5.27% and major assets reaching technical oversold levels, yet institutional whale flows show $325 million in Bitcoin moving off exchanges into self-custody while Ethereum saw large inflows to exchanges and stablecoin deposits. The desk's technical boards display golden crosses and severely depressed RSI readings across major assets, conditions consistent with capitulation lows, while leverage remains relatively calm and long-to-short ratios remain elevated. PCE data on Wednesday, November 25, will be the week's key data release; the Bitcoin difficulty adjustment, estimated at +8.94%, arrives in 643 blocks.
body: Crypto markets entered a sharp drawdown on Tuesday. Bitcoin down 5.27% over 24 hours and Bitcoin down 5.57% over seven days, with Ether down 6.94% over 24 hours and Ether down 6.05% over seven days tracking a broader liquidation environment. Solana down 9.52% over 24 hours and XRP down 8.46% over 24 hours extended the damage across alternative assets, while smaller-cap names showed steeper losses: ZEC down 17.35% over 24 hours, INJ down 13.65% over 24 hours, and QNT down 13.13% over 24 hours. The desk's Fear and Greed Index stands at 11, labeled Extreme Fear, the low end of its 30-day range of 10 to 51.

Institutional flows moved against the rally narrative. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $569.7M on the day, November 23, and spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows of $2,367.6M over the week through November 23. Ethereum flows turned sharply negative, with net outflows of $84.9M on November 23 alone and $382.3M over the last five sessions. Over the past week, however, the desk's Whale Watch board shows a more complex picture: $325,326,196 net moving off exchanges in Bitcoin, a sign consistent with self-custody or accumulation, while $148,818,693 net moving onto exchanges in Ethereum. The largest single Bitcoin withdrawal this week came from Kraken, $318.7 million, suggesting institutional or whale consolidation into custody, even as ETF holders trimmed positions.

Technical structure on the desk's boards shows mixed signals characteristic of capitulation lows. Bitcoin's RSI at 25.9 sits deep in oversold territory, below 30, and Ether's RSI at 29.0 is similarly depressed. Bitcoin is 16.1% below its 200-day simple moving average and 51.5% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81, yet the golden cross indicator is active on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and BNB, a signal that can precede recoveries. On the leverage side, per the desk's boards on OKX, BTC long-to-short ratio stands at 2.58 and ETH at 2.95, showing longs are significantly overextended relative to shorts. Funding rates across major assets remain near calm: Bitcoin 8-hour funding at 0.004% annualized, suggesting leverage is not at panic extremes, though liquidations in the past hour totaled $938,426 on BTC shorts and $577,208 on ETH longs.

Stablecoins moved onto exchanges alongside Ethereum, as $126,253,079 net moved onto Bitfinex alone, a pattern typically associated with traders preparing dry powder or hedging downside. Total stablecoin supply on the desk's boards stands at $283.2 billion, down 5.73% over 30 days. The network remains operational: Bitcoin difficulty adjustment is estimated at +8.94% with 643 blocks to the next retarget, and transaction fees are benign, the fastest fee at 2 sat/vB.

The week ahead carries economic data that may shape sentiment. On Wednesday, November 25, PCE: Personal Income and Outlays will publish, as the desk's calendar notes. Bitcoin's mining adjustment and broader macro calendars will shape the next 48 hours.
